description:
Conscious Lee is a passionate educator and cultural commentator known for dissecting myths surrounding Black history and social justice. With a sharp focus on challenging narratives that seek to erase or diminish the impact of white supremacy, Lee confronts popular misconceptions such as the “complicity myth”—the idea that Africans are equally responsible for the horrors of the Atlantic slave trade. Through compelling storytelling and critical analysis, Lee emphasizes the power dynamics and distinctions often overlooked in mainstream conversations, highlighting how arguments about African complicity are used to obscure the unique benefits gained by white enslavers and to sidestep real accountability. Driven by a commitment to truth and clarity, Conscious Lee creates space for honest dialogue and historical reckoning.

Complicity Isn’t Equivalence

Throughout the episode, Conscious Lee makes clear that bringing up African complicity is used as a “gotcha” moment to shut down deeper conversations about systemic injustice. He draws a fresh parallel—we never hear “white people invaded other white countries” as a reason to excuse wars and atrocities within Europe. So why do so many ignore the diversity of African nations and tribes, and lump them all together?
